newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler director gobbles up shares - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler director gobbles up shares - WSJ.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. director John Neff bought $1.4 million of the auto maker's stock last month at a time when others on Wall Street were shying away from the shares, the Wall Street Journal said on Wednesday.
In its electronic edition, the Journal said Neff, a high-profile money manager, bought 50,000 shares on April 15 at prices ranging from $28.63 to $28.88 each.
The purchases came after Chrysler's stock price dropped amid concerns about slowing sales, a rising dollar and higher interest rates, the Journal said.
The purchases were outlined by Disclosure Inc., which processes all insider filings on behalf of the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Neff, who was out of the country, did not comment. A Chrysler spokesman said he bought the shares on the first day of the most recent 30-day period during which Chrysler executives and directors are allowed to trade shares.
Before the April purchase, Neff owned 33,944 Chrysler shares as of March 31, according to a proxy statement.
